reason: Return of control is the real Bedrock Agents feature that hands function name and parameters back to the caller so an existing on-prem client executes the action; Lambda-over-VPN is re-architecture, InvokeModel drops orchestration, and a Knowledge Base only retrieves.

Converse API gives a unified request/response shape across Claude, Nova, and Llama, so A/B testing needs only a model-ID swap; per-family adapters are the code they want to remove, batch is async, and SageMaker adds hosting overhead.

Prompt caching a cache checkpoint after the 8K static prefix reuses it across requests, cutting input cost and time-to-first-token without changing prompt text; 8K exceeds cache minimums. Other options do not address repeated static input.

Exponential backoff with randomized jitter is the AWS-recommended ThrottlingException handling and de-synchronizes concurrent retries; tight loops and fixed intervals recreate retry storms, fail-fast drops recoverable calls.

Defining the schema as a Converse tool and using tool use makes the model emit arguments conforming to the schema; plain-English JSON has no guarantee, high temperature reduces consistency, and streaming only changes delivery.

An embeddings model such as Amazon Titan Text Embeddings returns fixed-length dense vectors for nearest-neighbor search; a generation model outputs prose, Guardrails enforce policy, and tool use is function calling.

A Lambda function URL with response streaming forwards ConverseStream chunks incrementally with the least added infrastructure; REST API Gateway buffers the full body, so raising the timeout and buffering both defeat streaming, and batch is async.

Step Functions models sequential/conditional steps, retries, and error handling declaratively with a visual execution history; a monolithic Lambda hand-codes flow and risks timeouts, and EventBridge/SQS require building the logic and observability.

Wrapping the contract in XML tags cleanly marks it as data versus instructions, matching Claude prompt best practice; higher temperature adds randomness, no delimiters worsens confusion, and separate requests lose shared context.

Agent memory and session state retain conversational context so earlier turn details carry forward without manual re-sending; Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity, Guardrails enforce policy, and CloudWatch logging is observability only.

An idempotency key with conditional writes guarantees a repeated request maps to one result; temperature does not control system retries, swallowing an error does not stop a second charge, and a longer timeout does not dedupe.

A function schema (function definitions) lets you list name, description, and parameters with the least authoring and no REST spec; OpenAPI is heavier, SageMaker inference components are unrelated, and an IAM policy governs permissions not the action interface.

Associating a Bedrock Knowledge Base adds managed retrieval and citations with no custom service; fine-tuning is costly and gives no citations, pasting handbooks bloats the prompt, and returning raw PDF bytes leaves parsing/grounding to build.

A Service Quotas increase gives durable RPM/TPM headroom and backoff-with-jitter plus a cross-Region inference profile smooths spikes and distributes load; temperature and Lambda memory do not affect quotas, and InvokeModel shares the same account limits.

Tool use constrains output to the declared schema and prefilling the assistant turn with an opening brace steers Claude to valid JSON; raising temperature/top_p reduces predictability, schema-free prompting has no guarantee, and dropping the system prompt does nothing.

An action group (Lambda or return of control) performs ticket creation and an associated Knowledge Base supplies grounded, cited answers, covering both requirements; Provisioned Throughput, CloudWatch logging, and a profanity Guardrail satisfy neither.

Embedding each product with Titan and embedding the query then running Aurora pgvector similarity search delivers semantic matching on existing infrastructure; fine-tuning builds no vector index, SQL LIKE is keyword-only, and Guardrails cannot rank.
